title: Reinstating Your HomeGuard Homeowners Policy after Cancellation for Nonpayment
content:
These terms explain to the named insured when a cancelled HomeGuard Homeowners Policy can be put back in force.

## Which policies can be reinstated

Only a policy cancelled for nonpayment can be reinstated. A policy cancelled at the insured's request or for an underwriting reason is never reinstated, and an expired policy follows the HomeGuard renewal terms instead. The reason for the cancellation is the one recorded on the policy.

## What is required

All of the following must hold:

1. **On time.** The reinstatement request is made no later than the reinstatement window that starts on the cancellation date. The window is the package's reinstatement window in days, counted in calendar days from the cancellation date recorded on the policy as its closing date, and a request on the last day of the window is on time.
2. **Paid up.** Before the policy is reinstated, the payments received since the cancellation date must cover the amount due as of the request date together with the package's reinstatement fee. The amount due as of a date is the premium installments billed whose due date is on or before that date, together with fees assessed, returned payments, additional premium and refunds issued posted on or before it, less payments received, fees waived and return premium posted on or before it, never below 0.00.
3. **No loss.** The named insured has signed a statement of no loss covering the days since the cancellation date, as recorded on the insured's request.
4. **Once per term.** A policy is reinstated at most once per term.

## What reinstatement does

- Reinstatement is without a lapse: the original term and expiration date are unchanged.
- The package's reinstatement fee is charged.
- The cancellation credit posted at cancellation is reversed by one additional premium entry of the same amount, marked as a reinstatement reversal and tied to no endorsement, dated the reinstatement date.

## Window examples (hypothetical)

Cancellation date 3 June; hypothetical reinstatement window of 15 days, so the last day is 18 June.

| Request date | On time |
|---|---|
| 18 June (last day of the window) | yes |
| 19 June | no |

## Paid-up example (hypothetical)

Amount due as of the request date 520.00; reinstatement fee 25.00. Payments received since the cancellation date totalling 545.00 satisfy condition 2; payments totalling 530.00 do not.
